rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When rejecters ignore God's warnings, He grants respite and opens the way to their demands; as they boast of success, their time expires and He suddenly seizes them.
rows.anchor: when those who have denied their messengers ignore such warnings from God, they are given more time by Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi glosses dābir as root, which grounds his image of a nation being uprooted.
rows.anchor: means “root.” The last verse means that before being uprooted

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the final punishment, trials only shake transgressors' branches temporarily while their roots remain safe; the final scourge uproots them.
rows.anchor: gusts of trials that visit such transgressors only shake the branches of their trees of existence and that too temporarily.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world has no benefit from a poisonous nation that bears poisonous fruit.
rows.anchor: there is no benefit left for the world in the tree that has become poisonous and is also bearing poisonous fruit.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Creator made the world to manifest mercy and justice, God cannot let a poisonous tree destroy His orchard; removing it makes Him worthy of gratitude.
rows.anchor: this world has been created by its merciful creator for a purpose and to manifest His mercy and justice in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fuller historical evidence for God's established practice is deferred to the next sūrah, which is a counterpart to this one.
rows.anchor: These details will be found in the next sūrah, which is a counterpart of the current one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next sūrah's history of Arabian nations destroyed by punishment shows that they too demanded signs and received bodily and financial trials to soften them and turn them to God.
rows.anchor: in order to soften their hearts and direct their attention to Himself, the Almighty inflicted them with various physical and financial trials.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those nations dismissed the trials as accidents instead of learning from them, so their rebellion brought full respite.
rows.anchor: Instead of drawing a lesson from them, they totally ignored them regarding them to be accidental happenings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan made repeated success seem proof that the nations were on the right path.
rows.anchor: They reaped success after success because Satan inveigled them into thinking that they were treading the path of success.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the nations were intoxicated by success, sudden punishment seized them and brought them to their senses.
rows.anchor: Ultimately when they were inebriated by their successes, divine punishment suddenly seized them and then they came to their senses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's rejecters and those demanding a punishment sign face the same pattern and will meet the same fate if they fail to learn.
rows.anchor: The implication of all this is that the Prophet’s rejecters and those who demand a sign of the punishment from him face the same phase.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to demands for punishment shifts from an external calamity, which none can stop, to an intellectual and internal affliction, from which only God can save.
rows.anchor: Now it is stated that if God inflicts them with some intellectual and internal punishment, none can save them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People currently fail to use their functioning sight, hearing, and understanding; if God removes these faculties, only He can restore them.
rows.anchor: if they are deprived of them by God, none except Him can restore them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rendered suddenly means an unexpected appearance, as from nowhere.
rows.anchor: means “suddenly” and “appearance of something out of the blue.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rendered openly means openly or in daylight.
rows.anchor: means “openly” and “in the light of day.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened punishment is for rejecting a messenger after the truth has been conclusively conveyed.
rows.anchor: is the punishment which visits people who deny their respective messengers after the truth is conclusively conveyed to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice is to destroy those who reject a messenger while saving the believers.
rows.anchor: The established practice of God regarding this punishment is that those who reject a messenger are destroyed and the believers are saved from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier trials and calamities affect everyone; believers benefit from them, while disbelievers persist in mischief and grow more stubborn.
rows.anchor: As for the trials and calamities mentioned earlier, they come to everyone regardless.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers manifest God's mercy: punishing people is not their purpose but the consequence of rejecting them.
rows.anchor: Punishing others is not the objective of their position; it is the consequence of denying them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should seek from messengers guidance about faith and righteous deeds, rather than asking them to bring what they warn people against.
rows.anchor: the messengers should be asked what they come for ie. guidance about faith and righteous deeds and not to bring forth what they have been sent to save people from.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles are neither a messenger's defining trait nor essential to preaching; God may manifest them when He wants to make the truth conclusive.
rows.anchor: working miracles is neither of their traits nor an essential ingredient of their preaching.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses comfort the Messenger to focus on glad tidings and warnings, leave matters outside his duty to God, and not worry without reason.
rows.anchor: these verses comfort the messenger that he should focus all his attention to his real purpose: delivering of glad tidings and warnings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not assume that present peace rules out punishment: God can seize them at any time and in any manner.
rows.anchor: He can seize them any time in any manner.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words about the people rejecting the truth mean that they reject the Qur'an's certain warning of punishment despite its truth.
rows.anchor: “and your people rejected it even though it is the very truth”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should leave the rejecters' matter to God and tell them he was not sent to force them to believe; his task is to warn and preach, which he has done.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should now leave their matter to God and inform them that he has not been sent to them to force them to accept faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to demands to hasten punishment, the Prophet should say that every event has its appointed time and will occur then.
rows.anchor: every event has a prescribed time in God’s calendar. It will happen when its time arrives.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When stubborn people engage in frivolous argument and mockery, the Prophet should leave them and speak only when they are receptive.
rows.anchor: When he sees that they are indulging in frivolous arguments and mockery, he should leave them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is preaching, not coercing belief; he should disregard new demands and give his warning through the Qur'an in the best way.
rows.anchor: His responsibility is just to preach and deliver the message. He is not responsible for their faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who wish to reform can do so without the believers being held responsible for the mockers' deeds; the believers' role is to remind them.
rows.anchor: Those who want to mend their ways will do so and not be taken to task because of their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No support, intercession, or payment can avail a person before God.
rows.anchor: No support, intercession or remuneration is of any avail before God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After receiving God's guidance, believers will not return to polytheism.
rows.anchor: the believers are not willing to even enter the whirlpool of polytheism once God’s guidance has come to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are called to submit to the Lord of the worlds, pray to Him, and fear Him alone.
rows.anchor: They have been asked to consign themselves to the Lord of the worlds, to pray to Him and to fear Him only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration leaves people free to adopt this path or wander away.
rows.anchor: Anyone who wishes can adopt this path and is also free to wander about.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration closes the possibility of further debate over the matter.
rows.anchor: The implied meaning is that now there is no question of any debate in this matter in the wake of this declaration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe's purposeful creation shows that the hereafter must come.
rows.anchor: At the end, the purposeful nature of this universe is indicated. Evident from it is that the hereafter is bound to come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day God alone will decide matters, and He is wise and knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: On that day, it is God alone Who will decide matters. He is wise and knowledgeable.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment will expose truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood; if people still refuse to listen, the Prophet should leave their matter to them.
rows.anchor: On that day everyone will know the truth to be true and falsehood to be false.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawḍ literally concerns entering into something and idiomatically means frivolous talk, hair-splitting, and baseless criticism that dismisses a subject by ridicule; the author cites Qur'anic usage including 9:65.
rows.anchor: It means to engage in frivolous talk, hair-splitting and baseless criticism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about treating religion as sport clarifies the point of khawḍ in these verses; the author also points to 4:140 as an explanation of the word.
rows.anchor: In other words after mentioning the word, its purpose has been elucidated.
